title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis and Purification of Bioorthogonally Tagged UDP‐GlcNAc and UDP‐GalNAc Analogues
author: Bineva‐Todd, Schumann

steps.title: Analytical‑scale screening of analogues
steps.instruction: Mix each GlcNAc or GalNAc analogue with bacterial kinase NahK (B. Longum, Chemily Glycoscience), inorganic phosphatase PmPpA (P. Multocida, Chemily Glycoscience), and either AGX1 WT or AGX1 F383A in 2× reaction buffer together with ATP and UTP; incubate for 16 h; analyse turnover by LC‑MS and select the AGX1 variant that gives the highest UDP‑sugar formation for preparative scale.

steps.title: Prepare preparative reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Using 2× reaction buffer, combine the chosen substrate analogue, ATP, UTP at the concentrations prescribed in the protocol, and single‑use enzyme aliquots of NahK, PmPpA and the selected AGX1 variant (stored at –80 °C to minimise freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Incubate enzymatic reaction
steps.instruction: Allow the preparative reaction to proceed for 16 h (≈1 day) at the recommended temperature; expect 30–50 % conversion of the analogue to the UDP‑sugar.

steps.title: Quench, CIAP treatment and desalting
steps.instruction: Quench the reaction as appropriate, add calf intestinal alkaline phosphatase (CIAP) and incubate for an additional day to dephosphorylate residual phosphates; then dry the reaction mixture by lyophilisation before desalting.

steps.title: Solid‑phase extraction on C18
steps.instruction: Secure a C18 SPE cartridge on a retort stand with a clamp; equilibrate by passing 50 ml acetonitrile followed by 50 ml deionized (or HPLC‑grade) water, discarding the flow‑through; place a rack of test tubes beneath the column; dissolve the lyophilised reaction residue in 0.5–2 ml water and load onto the cartridge; wash with 20 ml deionized water, collecting the flow‑through in 2–5 ml fractions; elute the product with 20 ml of 20–50 % (v/v) acetonitrile in water (choose the % based on analytical LC‑MS, e.g., 30 % if the product elutes at ~30 % ACN), again collecting 2–5 ml fractions; enzymes and salts are removed during this SPE step.

steps.title: Identify product fractions by TLC
steps.instruction: Spot all collected fractions—including the load, water wash, and acetonitrile eluate—on a TLC plate, develop, and locate the fractions that contain the UDP‑sugar product.

steps.title: Combine and lyophilise product fractions
steps.instruction: Pool all fractions identified as containing pure product and dry the combined pool by lyophilisation.

steps.title: Set up HPLC gradient and run purification
steps.instruction: Program the HPLC with a gradient based on analytical LC‑MS (e.g., if the product elutes at ~10 % ACN, use 0–15 % buffer B over 10 min or column volumes); use a flow rate of 25 ml/min and the same buffers as analytical LC‑MS; dissolve the semipure product in 0.2–0.5 ml water, inject, and run the column (multiple injections may be required depending on loading capacity); employ a mass‑directed autopurification (MDAP) C18 column (typical flow 25 ml/min) so that collection is triggered by the target mass, eliminating the need for post‑run LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Combine pure HPLC fractions and dry
steps.instruction: Collect all mass‑directed pure fractions, combine them, and remove solvent by lyophilisation to obtain the final >95 % pure UDP‑GlcNAc or UDP‑GalNAc analogue.
